items.script: I want to be straight with you, because I do not think vague feedback helps anyone. The delivery work has been excellent and nobody disputes that. items.script: My problem with the phrase is not that it is rude, it is that it has stopped meaning anything. Ten years ago it described a specific thing. Now it gets attached to whatever the speaker dislikes, which means when something genuinely fits the description, nobody hears it. We have spent the word. That is the loss, and you do not get it back by using it more carefully from now on.

items.script: The advice I keep hearing is to start small, and I think it is half right. Starting small works for the doing. It does not work for the deciding, and the deciding is where most people actually fail. If you have to choose each morning whether today is a running day, you have already spent the willpower before you reach the door. Make the decision once, in advance, and let the small version be what you do on the bad days.

questions.prompt: What does the speaker think starting small is good for?
Where does the speaker say people actually fail?
What is their recommendation?
